sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers the south-western corner of West New York, west of Bergenline Avenue, between Fifth Street and Farnam Avenue, crossed diagonally by Hudson Boulevard West. North points towards the upper right. Bergenline Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet; beyond it only the ends of 5th to 9th Streets and Klotz Lane are sketched, belonging to sheet 37. From Bergenline Avenue the narrow streets of an older, irregular layout run up the sheet: Fifth Street at the left edge, Surgent Street, Sheehan's Lane, which bends near its upper end, and Farnam Avenue at the right, with Maakens Street leaving Farnam Avenue for sheet 41. Hudson Boulevard West, 80 feet wide, cuts across the upper half from Fifth Street to the top right corner, and Fisher Avenue continues Surgent Street beyond it; the land north of the boulevard is blank. The blocks are divided into long narrow lots, many still empty. Buildings are mostly small one- and two-storey frame dwellings with sheds and stables, a few brick and stone outbuildings, and along Bergenline Avenue a row of frame shops including a hay and feed store and a blacksmith's shop. A dancing platform with an open shed stands in the block between Fifth and Surgent Streets, and a three-storey frame building faces the boulevard. Water mains of 6, 12 and 24 inches are marked in the streets. Unlike the other sheets of this atlas the sheet is drawn at 80 feet to an inch, with its own scale bar.
notes: Printed scale 80 ft to an inch (fitted 4.89 px per ft, consistent with the 60 ft sheets at 6.56).

Modern names, from junction spacing along Bergenline Avenue: Fifth Street is 49th Street, Surgent Street (and Fisher Avenue beyond the boulevard) is 51st Street at its western node, Sheehan's Lane is about 53rd Street and Farnam Avenue is 54th Street; Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard. The stubs 5th to 9th Street east of Bergenline Avenue are today's 49th to 53rd Streets; modern 51st Street jogs across Bergenline Avenue, with nodes 38 m apart.
Modern 52nd Street meets Bergenline Avenue about 18 m from the drawn 8th Street stub; that point was left out.

Map, 80 ft (printed). Union Hill / West New York line: Hudson Boulevard West (JFK Boulevard) crossing from Fifth Street to the top right, Bergenline Avenue along the bottom, Fifth Street, Surgent Street, Fisher Ave., Sheehan's Lane, Farnam Avenue, Maakens St.; 5th to 9th St. and Klotz Lane stubs below Bergenline. North to the upper right. One part. Configured by lead: 3 detected + 6 dashed/hand-picked points; 8th St. stub (52nd) left out (18 m off).

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the south-western corner of West New York, on the Town of Union boundary, between Bergenline Avenue on the west and Palisade Avenue on the east. The numbered streets run across the page, Fifth Street at the bottom and Wallace Street at the top, so north points towards the upper left. The southernmost strip, between a heavy boundary line lettered as the line between West New York and the Town of Union and the lower edge of the sheet, holds a few frame dwellings at the Bergenline end and narrow empty lots beyond. North of it the blocks along Sixth and Seventh Streets are partly built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, stables and sheds on narrow numbered lots, mostly facing the streets rather than the avenues. Eighth Street is laid out with dashed outlines and has almost no buildings. Between Ninth Street and Wallace Street the blocks are crossed by Klotz Lane, a narrow lane lettered in two places, with detached dwellings along it and a larger block of lots strung out between Klotz Lane and Wallace Street. Dashed block lines mark the unbuilt ground east of Klotz Lane and along Ninth Street. West of Bergenline Avenue the sheet repeats the edge of neighbouring sheets, with Surgent Street, Sheehan's Lane and Farnam Avenue, and the compass rose and a scale note at the left. The street widths are lettered at the block corners (50, 60 and 80 feet). Neighbouring sheets are keyed 36, 41, 43 and 38, and sheet 34 lies below the boundary strip. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Fifth to Ninth Streets east of Bergenline Avenue are today's 49th to 53rd Streets (Eighth Street is 52nd Street, whose modern node on Bergenline Avenue lies about 18 m from the drawn junction and was not used).
Surgent Street is today's 51st Street west of Bergenline Avenue; Farnam Avenue is 54th Street.
Wallace Street may be the western of the two 55th Street nodes at Palisade Avenue (it fitted there on neighbouring sheet 43); not certain. Klotz Lane has no known modern counterpart.
51st Street jogs across Bergenline Avenue in the modern street network (two nodes 38 m apart); the eastern node was used.

Map, 60 ft. Bergenline to Palisade Avenue, Fifth to Ninth Street (49th-53rd), Klotz Lane and Wallace Street to the north; Town of Union boundary strip at Fifth Street. North to the upper left (rotation about -31). One part. Helper: 3 detected + 5 dashed-tool points.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 covers the southern end of West New York between Palisade Avenue along the top of the sheet, Hudson Avenue through the middle and Broadway along the bottom, from Fifth Street on the left to Eleventh Street on the right. North is towards the upper right. The district was almost entirely unbuilt in 1900: the blocks are drawn with dashed outlines, the conventional sign for platted but unbuilt land, and only a row of small two-storey frame dwellings on the east side of Fifth Street near the Union line, a pocket-book works at the Palisade Avenue end of the same block, and a single building at Seventh Street break the empty lots. Each block between the avenues is about 200 by 400 feet, and the streets are drawn 50 to 60 feet wide. Along Fifth Street a dash-dot line marks the boundary between West New York and the Town of Union, the neighbouring municipality to the south. At the top right a narrow 35-foot Wallace Street and Klotz Lane enter from the adjoining sheet 43 on the other side of Palisade Avenue. A compass rose stands in the block between Tenth and Eleventh Streets. Lot numbers and frontage dimensions are printed along every block face, which record the subdivision of the land even where nothing has yet been built. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and adjoins sheets 37, 43 and 44 across Palisade Avenue, 39 and 73 across Broadway, and 35 across Fifth Street.
notes: Fifth to Eleventh Streets are today's 49th to 55th Streets (old number plus 44); Palisade Avenue, Hudson Avenue and Broadway keep their names.

Nearly every block is drawn with dashed outlines (unbuilt land); the detector's solid-line test cannot read them, so most control points were measured with a dashed-line variant of the detector and entered as hand-measured points.
Boundary between West New York and Town of Union (now Union City) drawn along Fifth Street.

Map, 60 ft. Palisade Avenue, Hudson Avenue, Broadway crossed by Fifth to Eleventh Streets (modern 49th to 55th); Union boundary along Fifth Street. North to the upper right. One part. Pilot. Configured: 2 detected + 17 points from the dashed-line detector variant (B/tools/dashed_gcp.py).

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers the south-east corner of West New York on the top of the Palisades, from the Weehawken boundary to Eleventh Street, between Hudson Boulevard East and Broadway. The sheet is turned on the page: Hudson Boulevard East curves down the left side along the edge of the cliff, Bullsferry Road runs down the middle and Broadway along the right, the numbered streets run across the page, and north points towards the lower right. The dash-dot boundary between West New York and Weehawken crosses the top of the sheet. Eighth, Ninth, Tenth and Eleventh Streets run from Bullsferry Road to Broadway, and every block between them is drawn with dashed outlines, the sign for laid-out but unbuilt land; the strip between the road and the boulevard is not divided at all. The only building on the sheet is a small brick meter house just north of the Weehawken line, between the boulevard and Bullsferry Road, with water mains of 10 and 12 inches marked beside it. The boulevard is drawn 80 feet wide; Bullsferry Road is drawn with two edge lines about 80 feet apart, and the cross streets 50 feet wide. Keys on the margins point to sheet 73 (Weehawken) across the boundary, sheet 76 for the land below the cliff, sheet 38 across Broadway and sheet 40 beyond Eleventh Street. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (fitted rotation about 148 degrees).
Eighth to Eleventh Streets are today's 52nd to 55th Streets; Bullsferry Road is Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.

All block outlines are dashed, so no junction was detected automatically; all six control points were hand-picked on the street centres. Modern 52nd Street meets Park Avenue at a three-way junction with 51st Street about 40 m from where Eighth Street met Bullsferry Road, so that junction was not used.
The fitted scale is about 2.5 percent smaller than the 60 ft scale of the other sheets (6.39 against 6.56 px per ft).

Map, 60 ft. Bullsferry Road (Park Avenue) and Hudson Boulevard East (Boulevard East) with Eighth to Eleventh Streets ending at Bullsferry Road; West New York / Weehawken boundary at the top. North points down. One part. Turned: north to the lower right (rotation about 148). All blocks dashed; 6 hand-picked junctions on Broadway and Bullsferry Road (Park Av). Drawn about 2.5 percent small.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 covers the strip between Broadway and Hudson Boulevard East on the high ground at the north-east of West New York, from Eleventh Street on the west to Sixteenth Street on the east. The numbered streets run up the page and Broadway crosses the top, so north points towards the upper right. Bullsferry Road runs diagonally across the lower part of the sheet from left to right, drawn with two lines about 80 feet apart, and Hudson Boulevard East follows the cliff edge below it with its own pair of edge lines. The whole sheet is almost empty. The blocks between Broadway and Bullsferry Road are outlined with dashed lines, the sign for laid-out but unbuilt ground; only a few lots near Fifteenth Street are ruled in, with one small dwelling, and a short row of lots below Fourteenth Street. A band of land lettered Ravine Road crosses the blocks midway between Broadway and Bullsferry Road, cutting them in two. A single small building stands beside Bullsferry Road. South of the road the ground towards the boulevard is blank except for short lot lines, and a scale bar and a compass rose fill the left margin. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet and house-number ranges are lettered along the block faces. Neighbouring sheets are keyed 39 to the left, 44 above, 49 to the right, 50 and 76 and 77 below. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Eleventh to Sixteenth Streets are today's 55th to 60th Streets; Bullsferry Road is today's Park Avenue (80 ft pair of lines used); Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.
Ravine Road has no modern counterpart; the Park Avenue junctions with 55th to 59th Streets were placed from the 80 ft pair of Bullsferry Road lines.
Control comes mostly (8 of 12 points) from the dashed-line variant of the detector because the block outlines are dashed.

Map, 60 ft. Broadway to Hudson Boulevard East, Eleventh to Sixteenth Streets (55th-60th), Ravine Road (gone), Bullsferry Road (Park Avenue). Unbuilt. One part. Helper: 4 detected + 8 dashed-tool points.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows the southern end of the part of West New York that lies west of Bergenline Avenue, at 80 feet to an inch, which is coarser than most sheets of the volume. North points to the upper right. Bergenline Avenue runs up the left edge, and along the top Farnam Avenue, an 80-foot street, separates the built blocks from the area of sheet 36. Four short north-south streets, Maakens, Polk, King and People Streets, cut the ground into numbered blocks that run from Farnam Avenue to Harrison Street, with a second tier of blocks (numbered 6 and 7) between Harrison Street and Union Lane. Hudson Boulevard West crosses the sheet on a diagonal at the right and cuts off the ends of Farnam Avenue and Harrison Street. Building is sparse. A row of small frame dwellings stands along the Bergenline Avenue frontage near Farnam Avenue and further down, a few dwellings and stables are scattered in the blocks, and a marble and granite works and an ice house with its tank room stand near King Street and Hudson Boulevard West. East of Bergenline Avenue the stubs of Sheehan's Lane, Klotz Lane, Wallace Street and 11th, 12th and 13th Streets are lettered at the edge. The lower half of the sheet is mostly empty: Harold Avenue is drawn along the bottom with one row of narrow lots on its north side and a few houses beside Bergenline Avenue, and the ground between Union Lane and Harold Avenue is outlined but blank. The scale bar and a compass rose with a long north arrow are in the upper right, and neighbouring sheets 36, 37, 43, 42 and 117 are named in the margins.
notes: Farnam Avenue is today's 54th Street and Harrison Street is 55th Street; the 54th and 55th Street junctions with Madison Street, Polk Street, Jackson Street, Adams Street and Bergenline Avenue fit the sheet within about 1.5 m.
Maakens, Polk, King and People Streets are today's Madison, Polk, Jackson and Adams Streets (identified by block spacing from Bergenline Avenue); Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
11th, 12th and 13th Streets east of Bergenline Avenue correspond to modern 55th, 56th and 57th Streets (old number plus 44).
Harold Avenue was not used for control: it lies roughly 10 to 15 m from modern 57th Street.
The printed scale bar reads 1 inch = 80 feet, not 60 feet; the fitted scale is 4.89 pixels per foot, which agrees with 80 feet.
Union Lane and the 55th to 57th Street blocks below it are drawn outline only; no control points were taken there.

Map, 80 ft (printed; notes earlier said 60). West of Bergenline: Farnam Avenue (54th), Harrison Street (55th), Union Lane, Harold Avenue (57th, displaced 10-15 m, left out), Maakens (Madison), Polk, King (Jackson), People (Adams) Streets, Hudson Boulevard West. Turned (rotation about 149). One part; control only in the top third.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 covers the district west of Bergenline Avenue from Harold Avenue at the top down to Pierce Avenue at the bottom, at 80 feet to an inch, with north to the upper right. Bergenline Avenue is the left edge and Hudson Boulevard West the right edge, so the sheet is a band about 1,800 feet across. Almost all the building is concentrated in the bottom third, between the two ends of the sheet's one fully built row of blocks: Mechler, Maakens, Polk, King, People, Jefferson and Washington Streets run up from Pierce Avenue and are lined with small frame dwellings, with stores and the Town Hall at the Bergenline Avenue end, a church and a hay and feed store among them, and a silk dyer near People Street. Jefferson and Washington Streets continue north with building on their frontages until about the middle of the sheet. The large middle and upper areas are outlined in thin lines but unbuilt, and carry only lot lines; Harold Avenue is drawn along the top with a lumber yard (a lumber shed and stable) at the Bergenline end, a few houses and a blacksmith near Hudson Boulevard West, and an ice house south of the boulevard. East of Bergenline Avenue the ends of 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th Streets are lettered at the edge. Spring Street is lettered where it meets Hudson Boulevard West at the right. A compass rose with north arrow is at the upper right, and a scale bar stands on the left edge. Sheets 41, 43, 46, 45, 117 and 118 are named in the margins.
notes: Pierce Avenue is modern 61st Street; Mechler Street is Van Buren Place, Maakens Street is Madison Street, King Street is Jackson Street, People Street is Adams Street; Polk, Jefferson and Washington Streets keep their names, and Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard. The identification comes from matching the row of junctions along Pierce Avenue (spacing and count between Bergenline Avenue and the boulevard).
13th to 16th Streets east of Bergenline Avenue correspond to modern 57th to 60th Streets (old number plus 44).
The part is placed from the nine junctions along Pierce Avenue only (a helmert fit, RMSE under 1 m); there is no control away from that row, so the upper two thirds of the sheet are low confidence.
Harold Avenue was not used: it lies roughly 14 m from modern 57th Street.
Printed scale bar: 1 inch = 80 feet.

Map, 80 ft (printed). Harold Avenue to Pierce Avenue (61st) west of Bergenline: Mechler (Van Buren Place), Maakens, Polk, King, People, Jefferson, Washington Streets, Hudson Boulevard West; town hall. Turned (rotation about 148). One part; helmert from 9 points along Pierce Avenue, upper two thirds extrapolated: low-medium confidence.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers the north-east part of West New York between Bergenline Avenue along the top of the page and Palisade Avenue along the bottom, from Wallace Street on the left to Sixteenth Street on the right. The numbered streets run up and down the page and north points towards the upper right. Almost all of the ground is laid out but unbuilt: the blocks of Twelfth, Thirteenth and Fourteenth Streets are outlined with dashed lines and carry no lots or buildings. Development is confined to two places. At the left, a narrow strip between Wallace Street and a lane lettered 11th St. holds a few frame dwellings and the large Alliance Silk Mill. At the right, the blocks on either side of Fifteenth Street are ruled into narrow lots with a line of one- and two-storey frame dwellings and a few outbuildings facing the street, and Sixteenth Street is drawn with a solid and a dashed edge. Harold Avenue is lettered at the top, beyond Bergenline Avenue, and 14th and 15th Street labels appear at the right margin where the neighbouring sheet 47 takes over. A compass rose and the north arrow are at the upper left, and a 60-foot scale bar runs down the left margin. Street widths of 50 and 80 feet and house numbers are lettered on the block faces. Adjoining sheets are keyed 41, 42 and 37 on the left and top, 47 on the right, and 44 and 38 below. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Eleventh to Sixteenth Streets are today's 55th to 60th Streets.
Wallace Street appears to be the western of the two nodes of 55th Street at Palisade Avenue (118 ft west of the Eleventh Street line); this was inferred from the fit, not from a printed link.
Control comes from the dashed-line variant of the detector (about 8 of 11 points), because the unbuilt blocks have dashed outlines.
Map, 60 ft. Bergenline to Palisade Avenue, Wallace and 11th to Sixteenth Streets (55th-60th); silk mill. One part.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 shows the middle of the high ground in West New York between Palisade Avenue at the top of the page and Broadway at the bottom, with Hudson Avenue crossing the middle, from Eleventh Street on the left to Sixteenth Street on the right. The numbered streets run up the page and north points towards the upper right. The whole sheet is laid out but almost entirely unbuilt: every block is outlined with dashed lines, and the only buildings are two groups of small frame dwellings and sheds in the blocks on either side of Fifteenth Street, one group above Hudson Avenue and one below it, where the lots are ruled in. Street widths of 50 feet and house-number ranges are lettered along the blocks. At the right margin, beyond Sixteenth Street, a separate set of blocks is labelled with the cross streets 12th, 10th and 9th, where sheet 48 continues. A compass rose and the north arrow are at the lower left, with a scale bar and a note of the Princeton library stamp. Adjoining sheets are keyed 43 above, 38 to the left, 48 to the right and 40 below. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Eleventh to Sixteenth Streets are today's 55th to 60th Streets.
Control comes from the dashed-line variant of the detector (10 of 16 points), because the unbuilt blocks have dashed outlines.
Map, 60 ft. Palisade Avenue, Hudson Avenue, Broadway, Eleventh to Sixteenth Streets (55th-60th). Unbuilt. One part.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 is the north-west corner of West New York where it meets North Bergen, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right while the lettering runs up the page. Pierce Avenue is the left edge, with Oak Street 1,200 feet to the right. Four long streets run across the sheet: Washington Street, Jefferson Street (called First Street east of the street gap at the middle), People Street (called Second Street east of the gap) and King Street (called Third Street east of the gap). The blocks between them are densely lotted, with small frame dwellings and stables on nearly every lot and several larger buildings, among them a bakery and the West New York Chapel of the Grove Reformed Church on the People Street block near Pierce Avenue. Hudson Boulevard West enters at the top left and crosses diagonally to the right edge, 80 feet wide, with a wedge-shaped block of lots between it and Washington Street. North of the boulevard, Robert Street, Danielson Street, South Street and Smith Avenue are lettered and a block of lots numbered 4 is drawn; Bergenwood Avenue branches off on the right. The names West New York and North Bergen are printed at the top right. A compass rose with a long north arrow stands at the top, and a scale bar is on the left. The adjacent sheets named in the margins are 42, 46, 51, 121 and 122.
notes: Pierce Avenue is modern 61st Street and Oak Street is 65th Street; Washington, Jefferson and King Streets keep their names, People Street is Adams Street and King/Third Street is Jackson Street; Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard. Identified by block spacing and by the fit of the Pierce Avenue and Oak Street junctions (RMSE 0.5 m).
The cross street drawn between the blocks about two fifths of the way across (modern 62nd Street) is only a lot line on this sheet; no control was taken there.
Washington Street ends against the south edge of the boulevard here, while the modern Washington / 62nd / Kennedy node lies about 16 m away; that junction was left out.
Smith Avenue and Bergenwood Avenue north of the boulevard exist today with the same names; Danielson Street, South Street and Robert Street were not matched.
Printed scale bar: 1 inch = 60 feet.

Map, 60 ft. North-west corner: Pierce Avenue (61st) to Oak Street (65th), Washington, Jefferson/First, People/Second, King/Third Streets, Hudson Boulevard West; North Bergen streets (Robert, Danielson, South, Smith, Bergenwood) beyond the boulevard, without control. One part.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 shows the blocks west of Bergenline Avenue between Pierce Avenue and Ferry Road, at 60 feet to an inch. It is turned like sheet 45, with north to the upper right, Bergenline Avenue along the bottom and Pierce Avenue up the left edge. Four long streets cross the sheet: King Street (Third Street east of the gap in the middle), Polk Street (Fourth Street), Maakens Street (Fifth Street) and Mechler Street, each running from Pierce Avenue to a break about two thirds of the way across, then continuing as a numbered street with offset blocks. The blocks are narrow lots built up with small frame dwellings and stables on the left, thinning out towards the right where the lots are drawn without buildings. Public School No. 10 stands in the middle of the Polk to Maakens block, and engine companies No. 2 and No. 1 are near Pierce Avenue and Bergenline Avenue; a blacksmith and a junk yard are on Mechler Street. At the right edge Ferry Road runs down from Fourth Street to Bergenline Avenue, and Oak Street leads off the top right where it meets 3rd Street. Below Bergenline Avenue Niles Avenue and 18th, 19th and 20th Streets are lettered at the edge. A compass rose with north arrow and a scale bar are drawn on the right and left. Sheets 42, 45, 47, 51 and 53 are named in the margins.
notes: Pierce Avenue is modern 61st Street, Ferry Road is 64th Street, and Oak Street is 65th Street; Mechler Street is Van Buren Place, Maakens/Fifth Street is Madison Street, Polk/Fourth Street is Polk Street, King/Third Street is Jackson Street. Identified by spacing from Bergenline Avenue and by the junction fit (RMSE about 1.1 m).
Niles Avenue and 18th, 19th and 20th Streets east of Bergenline Avenue are 61st, 62nd, 63rd and 64th Streets (old number plus 44).
The break between the two halves of each street (about two thirds of the way across) is a lot line or narrow gap with no cross street drawn; the modern 62nd Street junctions there were not used.
Third Street jogs about 9 m at Oak Street; the junction was taken on the eastern part.
Printed scale bar: 1 inch = 60 feet.
Map, 60 ft. Pierce Avenue (61st) to Ferry Road (64th) and Oak Street (65th) west of Bergenline: King/Third, Polk/Fourth, Maakens/Fifth, Mechler Streets. One part.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers the northern end of the West New York grid between Bergenline Avenue along the top and Palisade Avenue along the bottom, from Sixteenth Street on the left to Nineteenth Street on the right, with Niles Avenue running through the middle. The streets between the avenues run up and down the page and north points towards the upper right. Three cross streets, Fifteenth, Fourteenth and Thirteenth, run parallel to the avenues and divide the area into blocks numbered 1 to 6. Building is limited to the blocks beside Bergenline Avenue, where frame dwellings and a few stores stand on narrow lots, to scattered dwellings along Eighteenth and Nineteenth Streets, and to the grounds of the West New York Field Club, drawn near the lower left with a grand stand and bleachers. Most blocks are ruled into empty lots and several edges are dashed. Pierce Avenue is lettered above Bergenline Avenue at the top, the two avenues are lettered at the margins, and a compass rose, the north arrow and a 60-foot scale bar fill the left side. Lot numbers, widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet and house numbers are lettered along the block faces. Neighbouring sheets are keyed 42 and 46 above, 43 to the left, 53 to the right and 48 below. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Sixteenth, Niles Avenue, Eighteenth and Nineteenth are today's 60th, 61st, 62nd and 63rd Streets; Fifteenth, Fourteenth and Thirteenth Streets have no modern counterpart in the streets used.
61st Street jogs across Bergenline Avenue in the modern network: the western node corresponds to Pierce Avenue and the eastern node to Niles Avenue; both were detected.
The detected 61st Street / Bergenline Avenue point on the Niles Avenue side sits about 15 ft from the drawn street centre; residual is small.

Map, 60 ft. Bergenline to Palisade Avenue, Sixteenth (60th), Niles Avenue (61st), Eighteenth, Nineteenth (62nd, 63rd); cross streets Thirteenth to Fifteenth (no modern line); West New York Field Club grand stand. One part.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers four columns of blocks in the north-eastern part of West New York, between Palisade Avenue at the top of the sheet and Broadway at the bottom, and between Sixteenth Street on the left and Nineteenth Street on the right. North points towards the upper right. Niles Avenue and Eighteenth Street divide the area into blocks numbered 7 to 14, laid out in rows between Palisade Avenue, Hudson Avenue and Broadway; mid-block cross streets named Thirteenth, Twelfth, Eleventh, Tenth and Ninth Street are lettered along the rows. Most of the ground is unbuilt: the blocks east of Eighteenth Street are drawn only as dashed outlines with long lot lines, and the block between Hudson Avenue and Broadway beside Nineteenth Street has no buildings at all. Development is concentrated in the strip either side of Niles Avenue, where small frame dwellings, outbuildings and a few stables stand on narrow lots, among them a kindling wood yard in block 9. The one large structure is the grand stand of the West New York Field Club in the top left corner, drawn as an irregular yellow building beside Sixteenth Street. Street widths are lettered at the corners, 60 feet for most streets and 50 feet for Broadway and parts of Palisade Avenue. Dewey Avenue enters from the right edge. The margin keys name the adjoining sheets: 47 above, 49 below, 44 to the left and 53 and 55 to the right. A scale bar at the lower left gives 60 feet to an inch, and a compass rose in the upper right shows north.
notes: Old Sixteenth Street, Niles Avenue, Eighteenth Street and Nineteenth Street are today's 60th, 61st, 62nd and 63rd Streets; Palisade Avenue, Hudson Avenue and Broadway keep their names.
The rows of Thirteenth to Ninth Street have no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; only the avenues and the four cross streets were used as control.
Hand-picked control: the detector paired Sixteenth Street (drawn 80 feet wide, with a thin centre line) with the wrong lines, and the street edges on the unbuilt side are dashed.
Map, 60 ft. Palisade Ave / Hudson Ave / Broadway rows, Sixteenth to Nineteenth Streets and Niles Avenue (60th-63rd); Sixteenth drawn 80 ft with a centre line, its points hand-picked. One part.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 lies directly below sheet 48 in the north-eastern part of West New York and shows the ground between Broadway at the top and Bullsferry Road across the bottom, from Sixteenth Street at the left to Nineteenth Street at the right. North points towards the upper right. Niles Avenue and Eighteenth Street cross the sheet, forming blocks numbered 15 to 20 in three rows separated by Ninth Street (lettered along Broadway), Eighth Street and North Street. The area above Broadway is blank because it belongs to sheet 48. Building is thin and clustered along Niles Avenue and in the south-west corner. Block 15 holds a school, drawn in pink, with frame dwellings and a stable beside it; block 16 has a short row of small dwellings on Ninth Street; block 17 carries scattered frame dwellings, outbuildings and sheds along Niles Avenue; and block 20 has a row of attached two-storey frame dwellings with stepped fronts facing Bullsferry Road. At the lower left, a range of open sheds and a hay and feed store stands on the corner of Sixteenth Street and Bullsferry Road. The blocks east of Eighteenth Street are drawn as dashed outlines with long lot lines and no buildings. Bullsferry Road runs slantwise across the foot of the sheet and is drawn with two sets of edge lines, dimensioned 60 and 80 feet, converging towards the east. Streets are lettered 50 or 60 feet wide, Sixteenth Street 80 feet. A compass rose at the lower left shows north, and a scale bar on the left margin gives 60 feet to an inch. Keys give the neighbouring sheets as 48 above, 50 below, 40 to the left and 55 to the right.
notes: Old Sixteenth Street, Niles Avenue, Eighteenth Street and Nineteenth Street are today's 60th, 61st, 62nd and 63rd Streets; Eighth Street matches Buchanan Place by spacing (about 250 feet from Broadway); Bullsferry Road is Park Avenue; Broadway keeps its name.
North Street (about 400 feet from Broadway) has no modern counterpart with more than one junction and was not used.

The Park Avenue control points are medium confidence: Bullsferry Road is drawn with 60 and 80 foot lines that converge towards the east, so its centre was placed 235 px above the lowest line; they agree with the Broadway and Eighth Street points to about 1.5 m.

The detector gave inconsistent points on Sixteenth Street (drawn 80 feet with a thin centre line) and on Bullsferry Road, so all junctions except 61st Street at Broadway and at Eighth Street were hand-picked.
Map, 60 ft. Broadway, Eighth Street (Buchanan Place), North Street, Bullsferry Road (Park Avenue); Sixteenth to Nineteenth Streets. One part; Park Avenue points hand-picked, medium confidence.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 shows the nearly empty high ground of north-east West New York between Bullsferry Road and Hudson Boulevard East, from Sixteenth Street to Twentieth Street. North points towards the upper right. Bullsferry Road crosses the top of the sheet; beyond it only the ends of Sixteenth Street, Niles Avenue and Eighteenth, Nineteenth and Twentieth Streets are drawn, with dashed block outlines. Hudson Boulevard East enters from the left, bends sharply towards the river, runs down the sheet and bends again to continue along the bottom edge, a jog of the boulevard towards the edge of the cliff. Between the road and the boulevard the land is blank apart from two long dashed property lines; the only buildings are a handful of small frame dwellings and outbuildings on Bullsferry Road near Sixteenth Street, at the top left. Bullsferry Road is drawn about 60 feet wide, with an additional dashed line marking a wider line of 80 feet. Keys on the margins point to sheet 40 to the south-west, sheet 49 across Bullsferry Road, sheet 57 to the north-east and sheets 77 and 78, the waterfront below the cliff. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old 16th, 18th, 19th and 20th Streets are today's 60th, 62nd, 63rd and 64th Streets; Niles Avenue is 61st Street; Bullsferry Road is Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.
Placed from five junctions along Park Avenue only (two detected, three hand-picked), so the transformation is a similarity (helmert); the boulevard side of the sheet is extrapolated.

Map, 60 ft. Bullsferry Road and Hudson Boulevard East between Sixteenth and Twentieth Streets; almost blank. One part. Configured: helmert from 5 junctions along Bullsferry Road (Park Av, 60th-64th; Niles Ave = 61st); boulevard side extrapolated.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 lies on the west side of Bergenline Avenue and straddles the boundary between West New York and Guttenberg, which is printed across the sheet as a line lettered Boundary between West New York and Guttenberg. The sheet is turned on the page, with north towards the lower right: the cross streets (Ferry Road, Oak Street, Cedar Street, Towerhill Avenue and Hudson Avenue) run across the page, the numbered streets run up and down, and Bergenline Avenue closes the left edge. In the upper, West New York part, Fifth, Fourth, Third and Second Streets divide blocks numbered 1 to 6; most of the lots are long and narrow, and development is a scatter of frame dwellings with a close row of attached dwellings along Fourth Street. A church and school stand in block 1 beside Oak Street. Cedar Street is crossed by a long unbroken strip of narrow lots on its south side that reaches to Hudson Boulevard West at the right, where the road curves along the edge of the Palisades. South of the boundary, in the Guttenberg part, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh and Eighth Streets run down to Hudson Avenue, and Towerhill Avenue crosses above them. This part is more built up: rows of frame dwellings face Towerhill Avenue, a large hall with open sheds stands at its east end, and dwellings, stables and sheds fill blocks 3, 6, 9 and 12. A large block in the lower-left centre of the sheet is left blank. The margins carry lettering of adjoining sheets, among them 20th to 23rd Streets beside sheet 53 and Towerhill Avenue beside sheet 45, with the keys 46, 45, 122, 52, 53 and 54. A scale bar at the left margin gives 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (fitted rotation about 149 degrees).

By block spacing along Bergenline Avenue: Ferry Road is 64th Street, Oak Street is 65th Street, Cedar Street is 66th Street, Towerhill Avenue is 67th Street and Hudson Avenue (Guttenberg) is 68th Street.

Fifth Street (upper) and Fifth Street (lower) are Madison Street; Fourth and Sixth Streets are Polk Street; Third and Seventh Streets are Jackson Street; Second and Eighth Streets are Adams Street; Hudson Boulevard West is John F. Kennedy Boulevard.
66th Street / Bergenline Avenue was rejected by the detector (10 m): the modern node is displaced from where Cedar Street meets Bergenline Avenue.
65th Street / Polk Street (Oak Street does not cross Fourth Street on the sheet) and 67th Street / John F. Kennedy Boulevard (curved boulevard edges, 3.5 m) were left out.
The boundary line between West New York and Guttenberg runs across the sheet just south of the Towerhill Avenue blocks, at the head of Fifth to Eighth Streets (lower part).

Map, 60 ft, turned (rotation about 149). West of Bergenline at the Guttenberg line: Ferry Road (64th), Oak (65th), Cedar (66th), Towerhill Avenue (67th), Hudson Avenue (68th); Guttenberg Fifth to Eighth Streets (Madison, Polk, Jackson, Adams). 66th / Bergenline left out (modern node about 18 m off). One part.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 shows three long north-west to south-east blocks of West New York between Hudson Avenue on the left, Palisade Avenue in the middle and Bergenline Avenue on the right, crossed by Nineteenth, Twentieth, Twenty-First, Twenty-Second and Twenty-Third Streets. The sheet is turned on the page: the numbered streets run across it with their numbers increasing downwards, the avenues run up and down, and north points towards the lower right, as the compass rose at the right margin shows. The blocks are numbered 1 to 6 and are cut into long narrow lots by closely spaced lot lines. Most of the ground is unbuilt. Building is concentrated in two places: a row of detached frame dwellings along the south side of Block 2 facing Twenty-First Street, and, in the bottom row of blocks beside Twenty-Third Street, a cluster of small dwellings and sheds. The largest structure is the Landau Silk Mill, a pink-shaded works with skylights in the roof, standing in Block 3 between Hudson and Palisade Avenues, with a small engine house beside it and a row of dwellings on the other side of the block. A few stables and outbuildings stand east of Palisade Avenue, and a larger frame house and its outbuildings near Bergenline Avenue. Bergenline Avenue is drawn 80 feet wide and the other streets 50 or 60 feet. The right margin carries the lettering of the adjoining sheet, with Ferry Road and Cedar Street and the sheet numbers 46 and 51. Keys name the neighbouring sheets as 47 and 48 above, 54 and 56 below and 55 to the left. A scale bar at the left margin gives 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Nineteenth to Twenty-Third Streets are today's 63rd to 67th Streets; Hudson, Palisade and Bergenline Avenues keep their names.
Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (fitted rotation about 149 degrees).
66th Street / Bergenline Avenue was left out: the modern node lies about 18 m from where Twenty-Second Street meets Bergenline Avenue on the sheet.

63rd Street / Bergenline Avenue and 63rd Street / Palisade Avenue were hand-picked because the detector paired the wrong lines at the top edge of the sheet; the modern 63rd Street is about 3 m off the drawn Nineteenth Street there.
Landau Silk Mill (Block 3) stood between Hudson and Palisade Avenues south of Twenty-Second Street.
Map, 60 ft, turned (rotation about 149). Hudson, Palisade, Bergenline Avenues crossed by Nineteenth to Twenty-Third Streets (63rd-67th). 66th / Bergenline left out. One part.

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows the north end of West New York between Bullsferry Road on the left and Hudson Avenue on the right, crossed by Nineteenth, Twentieth, Twenty-First, Twenty-Second and Twenty-Third Streets. The sheet is turned on the page: the numbered streets run across it with their numbers increasing downwards, the other streets run up and down, and north points towards the lower right, as the compass rose at the lower left shows. Bullsferry Road runs down the left side as a slightly slanted band, with a second pair of lines marking a proposed 80 foot width beside the existing 60 foot road. Broadway, 60 feet wide and widening to 80 feet at the foot of the sheet, divides the large blocks to its left from the narrower ones to its right, and Dewey and Hudson Avenue follow at the right. Almost the whole sheet is unbuilt. Three very large blocks between Bullsferry Road and Broadway are outlined only with dashed lines and carry no lots or buildings, and the blocks numbered 7 to 9 and 4A to 6A east of Broadway are cut into narrow lots with no buildings drawn. Block 7 at the lower left is subdivided into narrow lots. At the bottom right, block 5 is split by a diagonal street lettered only Avenue, and block 7 and block 4A have curved edges where the street grid bends. No building of any kind is drawn. The margin keys give the neighbouring sheets as 49 and 48 above, 56 and 54 below, 57 to the left and 53 to the right. A scale bar at the left margin gives 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Old Nineteenth to Twenty-Third Streets are today's 63rd to 67th Streets; Bullsferry Road is Park Avenue; Dewey is today's Dewey Avenue; Hudson Avenue and Broadway keep their names.
Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (fitted rotation about 149 degrees).
The street running diagonally through block 5 at the lower right is lettered only Avenue; it is probably the bend of Dewey Avenue and was not used as control.
Dewey Avenue at 66th and 67th Streets was left out because the street bends there on the sheet and the modern junctions do not match the drawn ones.
Park Avenue control points (64th, 66th, 67th Streets) are medium confidence: they are the centre of the 80 foot Bullsferry Road lines, and sit within about 3 m of the modern junctions.
All control is hand-picked: the street edges are dashed on the unbuilt side and the detector gave points 4 to 7 m off.
Map, 60 ft, turned (rotation about 149). Bullsferry Road, Broadway, Dewey, Hudson Avenue crossed by Nineteenth to Twenty-Third Streets. Nearly all dashed/unbuilt; all 16 points hand-picked. One part.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers the north-east corner of West New York on the high ground between Hudson Boulevard East and Bullsferry Road, from Nineteenth Street to Twenty-Third Street. The sheet is turned on the page: Hudson Boulevard East runs down the left side and Bullsferry Road down the right side, the numbered streets run across the page, and north points towards the lower right. Almost the whole sheet is empty. North of Twenty-Second Street the land between the boulevard and the road is drawn without streets, lots or buildings, and the short ends of Nineteenth, Twentieth and Twenty-First Streets appear only beyond Bullsferry Road, outlined with dashed lines, the sign for laid-out but unbuilt blocks. The built part is a single strip of three blocks, numbered 2, 3 and 4, between Twenty-Second and Twenty-Third Streets, divided by Washington Place and Lincoln Place. It holds rows of small one- and two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, a few stables, and a larger frame house towards Bullsferry Road. The boulevard is drawn 100 feet wide and curves along the edge of the Palisades; Bullsferry Road is drawn with two sets of edge lines, marked 60 and 80 feet, apparently the existing road and a wider proposed line. Lot numbers and frontages are printed along the block faces. Keys on the margins point to sheet 50 to the south-west, sheet 55 across Bullsferry Road, sheet 58 (Guttenberg) across Twenty-Third Street, and sheet 78, the waterfront below the cliff. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch.
notes: Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (fitted rotation about 149 degrees).
Old 19th to 23rd Streets are today's 63rd to 67th Streets; Bullsferry Road is Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East; Washington Place is McKinley Place; Lincoln Place keeps its name.
The cross-street edges on the unbuilt side are dashed; the detector paired the solid edge with a lot line at two junctions on Twenty-Second Street, which were hand-picked instead.

Map, 60 ft. Bullsferry Road and Hudson Boulevard East, Nineteenth to Twenty-Third Streets; Washington Pl., Lincoln Pl. One part. Turned: north to the lower right (rotation about 149). Washington Pl = McKinley Place. 6 detected + 5 hand-picked.

sheet-77.description: Sheet 77 shows the southern part of the West New York waterfront below the Palisades, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, upside down relative to sheet 78: the Hudson River is on the left, Hudson Boulevard East runs along the top of the cliff down the right side and turns across the bottom of the sheet, and north points towards the lower right. Most of the sheet is open water and empty filled land. The shore line, partly made ground, runs down the middle; Broad Street, 80 feet wide, runs from the shore inland to the Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, which crosses the sheet diagonally at the foot of the cliff with the West Shore Railroad tracks beside it. At the top right the tracks fan out into the yard of the West Shore Railroad, and a box notes the West Shore Grain Elevator, drawn on sheet 76. The few buildings are a group of small dwellings and sheds around Broad Street and Stone Street near the turnpike, two small buildings at the water's edge north of Broad Street, and the ferry house with its bridge to the ferry slip at the bottom of the sheet, the same building that appears at the foot of sheet 78. The exterior (pier head) line is marked in the river. Keys on the margins point to sheet 76 to the south, sheets 40 and 50 on the cliff above, and sheet 78 to the north.
notes: Sheet turned on the page: north towards the lower right (rotation 148.5 degrees, taken from sheet 78 turned through 180 degrees and from sheet 57).

No street junction on the sheet survives: Broad Street and Stone Street are gone, and the turnpike (now River Road) and the waterfront have been rebuilt. Placed from one point carried from sheet 78 (the north-west corner of the ferry house, drawn on both sheets) with the printed scale (3.94 px per ft, 100 ft to an inch) and the rotation of the neighbouring sheets: very low confidence.
A box on the sheet refers to the West Shore Grain Elevator on sheet 76, which is not in this atlas.

Map, 100 ft (printed). Waterfront below the cliffs: Hudson River, Broad Street, Stone St., Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, West Shore Railroad, Hudson Boulevard East along the top of the cliff; ferry to 42nd St. One part. Turned: north to the lower right (148.5, sheet 78 turned through 180). No surviving junction; anchored on one corner carried from sheet 78 (ferry house) with printed scale; very low confidence.

sheet-78.description: Sheet 78 shows the West New York waterfront below the Palisades at its northern end, from the Guttenberg boundary southwards, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page, with the Hudson River along the right side and north towards the upper left. Hudson Boulevard East runs along the top of the cliff at the left edge, where Hudson Avenue, 23rd Street and 22nd Street meet it from beyond the sheet. Ferry Road descends the cliff at the top of the sheet, and along it runs the dash-dot boundary line between West New York and Guttenberg; Water Street leaves it northwards. The Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike runs down the sheet near the foot of the cliff, with the West Shore Railroad tracks beside it and a curving siding to the docks. The north end is the works of the W. J. Wilcox Lard and Refining Company: a large brick refinery, steam-out, boiler and engine house and filling and canning buildings, a fire-engine house, a frame storage building on a pier, and a yard of eleven oil tanks lettered A to K with a carpenter's shop, lumber shed and stable, connected by an open bridge at second-storey level across the turnpike. South of it are the coal pockets and coal trestle of the N.Y.O. and W. Railroad on slips filled into the river, then the Union Granite Company's long frame works and an ice house beside the tracks, a few dwellings on the slope, and near the bottom of the sheet the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad marine repair shop and the slip of the ferry to 42nd Street, New York. A printed note lists the refinery's automatic sprinklers, fire buckets, water casks and hose.
notes: Sheet turned on the page: north towards the upper left (fitted rotation about -31 degrees). Printed scale 100 ft to an inch.

Hudson Avenue (Guttenberg), 23rd Street and 22nd Street are today's 68th, 67th and 66th Streets; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East. The turnpike corresponds roughly to today's River Road, which has been rebuilt: its modern junction with Ferry Road lies about 15 m from the drawn one and was not used.

Placed from two junctions on Boulevard East only (68th and 66th Streets), as a similarity (helmert); 67th Street was left out on purpose so that three nearly collinear points would not give an exactly determined affine fit. The waterfront is extrapolated about 600 m from that control: low confidence.
The whole waterfront has been redeveloped (Port Imperial); none of the drawn works survive.

Map, 100 ft (printed). Waterfront below the cliffs, up to the Guttenberg line: W. J. Wilcox Lard & Refining Co., coal pockets and trestle, Union Granite Co., West Shore Railroad, Hoboken and Hudson River Turnpike, Ferry Road, Hudson Boulevard East. One part. Turned: north to the upper left (rotation about -31). Helmert from 68th and 66th St on Boulevard East (Hudson Ave = 68th, 23rd = 67th, 22nd = 66th); waterfront extrapolated; low confidence.
